mstts:express-as.prosody: As we wrap up our look at Nickel and Dimed, let's bring it all together. If you've been following along, you've seen just how tough it is to survive on minimum wage—no matter how hard someone works. The emotional weight of poverty isn't just about dollars and cents. It's about the constant worry, the tough choices, and the sense of isolation that so many people face every single day. Choices for the working poor? They're shaped by fear, not freedom. And the social stigma that comes with struggling to make ends meet—well, that only makes things harder. Sure, charity and government help can make a difference, but they don't get to the root of the problem. The truth is, poverty sends shockwaves through families, communities, and our whole society. Lasting change? It takes more than goodwill. It takes systemic solutions—ones that go beyond individual effort. So, what does all this mean for you? If these stories have moved you, let that feeling nudge you to really look at the world around you. Notice the people who serve your food, clean your hotel room, or stock those shelves. Support policies that lift wages, expand healthcare, and make housing within reach. Real change starts with seeing—really seeing—the people who keep our society running, and refusing to let their struggles go unnoticed. The road ahead isn't easy, but it's possible. And it starts with empathy, awareness, and the courage to demand better for everyone. Thanks for being part of this journey. Now, let's move forward—together.
